steps: Temperature: As temperature rises, enzyme activity increases up to an optimum temperature. Above the optimum, the enzyme’s shape changes (it is denatured), so its activity decreases or stops. Low temperature slows enzyme activity.
pH: Each enzyme works best at a particular optimum pH. A pH above or below this value changes the enzyme’s shape and reduces its activity; extreme pH can denature the enzyme.

Substrate concentration: Increasing substrate concentration increases the rate of the enzyme-controlled reaction while enzyme molecules are available. The rate reaches a maximum when all the enzyme molecules are occupied by substrate.
Enzyme concentration: Increasing enzyme concentration increases the reaction rate when sufficient substrate is available, because more enzyme molecules can act on the substrate.
Inhibitors: Inhibitors reduce or stop enzyme activity by interfering with the enzyme’s action.
items.finalAnswer: Enzyme activity is affected by temperature, pH, substrate concentration, enzyme concentration and inhibitors.
